question.problem: Mr. Smith owns a factory where pants are made. To make these pants, the factory has several sewing machines. Mr. Smith wishes to determine the rate at which the number of pants increases with the number of sewing machines. What is an appropriate unit for Mr. Smith's purpose?

current_example.problem: A tank is being filled with water. What is an appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank, as time goes on?
current_example.worked_solution:
We *measure the change* of the volume as *we change* the amount of time. Consequently, any appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank must take the form

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{unit of volume}}{\textrm{unit of time}}.
$$

Some examples of appropriate units include $\dfrac{\textrm{liters}}{\textrm{hour}},$ $\dfrac{\textrm{m}^3}{\textrm{min}},$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{cm}^3}{\textrm{s}}.$
